statement:
bray answers relay queries with a single REQ, both from the `relay-query` MCP tool and from the `req` CLI command. Relays cap how many events one REQ returns (commonly 100 to 500), so a large `limit` is silently truncated and the caller cannot tell a complete result from a partial one.

Intended change: add opt-in pagination. The `relay-query` tool gains `paginate` (boolean) and `max_pages` (integer) inputs; `req` gains `--paginate`, `--max-pages N` and `--paginate-interval MS`. When pagination is on, bray keeps issuing queries, walking `until` backwards, until `limit` events have been collected or the relay returns nothing new, with a default cap of 20 round-trips. Events that share a timestamp at a page boundary must be neither skipped nor returned twice. Pagination must work whether the query goes to the active identity's read relays or to explicitly given relay URLs, and on the CLI it must also apply when the filter is piped in on stdin. Separately, when `relay-query` runs without pagination and the result exactly fills the limit, its response must say that there may be more events.

Do not edit any files. Working from the base commit, work out: which source files and symbols must change and what each change is; which callers of the shared query path must change to pass the new options; and which callers of that path are unaffected and why. Back every claim with line ranges valid at the base commit.
answerFormat: Write answer.json containing one JSON object: {"mustChange": [{"path": string, "symbol": string, "change": string}], "affectedCallers": [{"path": string, "symbol": string, "impact": string}], "unaffected": [{"path": string, "symbol": string, "reason": string}], "evidence": [{"path": string, "startLine": number, "endLine": number, "claim": string}]}. Paths are repository-relative. Line numbers are 1-based and inclusive at the base commit. New helpers may be described by behaviour; their names are your choice.
